newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - German rate view weighs on Euromark vols.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - German rate view weighs on Euromark vols.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options on LIFFE was under pressure from the stable outlook for German interest rates this year, traders said on Tuesday.
They said activity in front-month Euromark futures has been outstripped at times by interest in the back or "red" months.
"Some days the red months are where the major activity is," said a trader at a U.S. house. "It's anticipating rates will be unchanged."
Volatility in June dipped under nine percent in early trade to 8.9 percent, traders said. September was steady at 10.5 and December was bid at 13.35 percent, down fractionally on the day.
A trader at a French house said one reason for the somewhat limited activity in Euromarks, and the consequent fall in vol, was a result of soaring volatility in the French short end.
He said Pibor was soaking up much of the investor interest in short-term European debt derivatives. French markets have been jolted by the move to hold snap elections in late May/early June.
"If you want short-term volatility, Pibor is the place to go, not Euromarks at the moment," the French house trader said.
A U.S. house sold 1,000 Euromark strangles -- with the puts at a strike of 96.50 and the calls at 96.75 in December. A European bank also bought 950 of the September calls at the 97.00 strike.
A trader at a German house said although volatility was low, traders were nervous of buying it at these levels.
Currently the German discount rate is 2.50 percent and the lombard rate is 4.50 percent.
June Euromark futures were up 0.01 at 96.75 while September was unchanged at 96.69 at 0958 GMT.
